records.name: Share Food Program
records.summary: A Philadelphia food bank that supplies more than 280 partner pantries and community groups, delivers boxes to seniors, and runs a free community fridge and pantry at its warehouse on Hunting Park Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Pack boxes of food for seniors or the partner pantry network, call seniors to confirm deliveries, help at a food distribution site, care for produce at Nice Roots Farm, or speak up on issues as an advocate.

locations.label: Share warehouse and Share Community Fridge and Pantry

first_step.how: Open the volunteer page, pick a role (packing, calling, farming, pantry support, or advocacy), then email volunteer@sharefoodprogram.org or call (215) 223-2220 to learn the next open shift
first_step.basis: Several roles and a public volunteer email are listed for anyone to use, though the page gives no shift days or times

records.notes: Also runs Philly Food Rescue, which has its own record. The Community Fridge and Pantry at the warehouse opened in 2024 and is open around the clock with free food. The site says there are more than 30 community fridges citywide but does not say how many Share runs. The newest dated item is a news piece dated August 21, 2026 on the home page; its own URL was not captured. Court-ordered and service-hours status are not stated on the pages read. The Find Food map and locator were not used (browser tool).

records.name: Philly Food Rescue
records.summary: A Share Food Program branch where volunteers pick up surplus food from grocers, restaurants and farmers markets, then deliver it to nearby pantries, senior centers and community fridges.
records.what_you_do: Claim a food rescue in the app, pick up the food by car, bike or on foot, drop it at the matched recipient, and record the rescue in the app. Each rescue takes about an hour or less.

schedule.text: Rescues are posted in the app as they come up. They can be one time or recurring, and each takes about an hour or less.

first_step.how: Download the Philly Food Rescue app from the App Store or Google Play, create a profile, turn on notifications, and claim a rescue
first_step.basis: Anyone can join through the app and the page lists the steps, but it does not say that beginners are welcome

records.notes: Kept as its own record because it has its own sign-up path. Requirements on the page: a valid driver's license and car insurance if driving, a bike or transit pass for smaller rescues, a cell phone, and the ability to lift 30 lbs (or bring a friend). The only dated item on the pages read is a 2023 statistic (396 volunteers), which does not show current activity, so status is probably_active rather than active. The phone number is Share's general line, not a dispatch line. Closed-toe shoes are required at the warehouse.

records.name: Mama-Tee Community Fridge Project
records.summary: A network of community fridges across Philadelphia, run with volunteers, that puts fresh food within reach of neighbors. It also runs a pop-up grocery store on Washington Avenue.
records.what_you_do: Help distribute fresh produce and organize donations, take part in school or company volunteer days, or work on projects remotely from home.

locations.label: St. Christopher's Hospital for Children (North Philly)
Opportunity Towers I and II (Nicetown, two fridges)
Community Partnership School (Strawberry Mansion and Brewerytown)
Fridge at a site the page does not name (Germantown)

first_step.how: Use the volunteer page's email button for the track you want (Volunteer Inquiry, Corporate or School Volunteer Inquiry, or Virtual Volunteer Inquiry). It opens a message to hello@mama-tee.com.
first_step.basis: Three volunteer tracks are listed openly with a direct email way in, but the page gives no shift days, times or training details

records.notes: The fridge page lists 16 sites that cover 18 fridges (Caribe Towers and Opportunity Towers I and II each have two). Five sites are marked on the page as out of order or relocating, so they are left off the location list: Zig Zag BBQ (2113 E York St), YMCA North Philly (1400 N Broad St), Castellino's Italian Market (1255 E Palmer St), Myers Recreation Center (5801 Kingsessing Ave, Kingsessing), and 308 N 39th St (relocating). The site gives no fridge hours or delivery schedule. The site's dates are image file names and a copyright footer, which do not count, so the 2025 date comes from the Inquirer guide. An Idealist listing (lead platform, not used as a source) describes Saturday shifts; that was not recorded.

records.name: The People's Fridge
records.summary: A West Philadelphia food project that gives out free groceries at pop-ups in Cedar Park and runs a warehouse that restocks community fridges across the city.

schedule.text: Free food pop-up at Cedar Park on the 2nd and 4th Saturday, 2 to 4 pm, as the homepage states. The site also says that since January 2026 it hosts bi-monthly pop-ups there.

first_step.how: The site lists no volunteer sign-up. Use the contact page at thepeoplesfridge.org/contact to ask how to help, or come to a Saturday pop-up.
first_step.basis: The site gives no volunteer steps or schedule, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: The get-involved page cited in the Inquirer guide returns 404, so no volunteer page was found. The Cedar Park location is given only as the corner of 50th Street and Baltimore Avenue. The Facebook and Instagram accounts are not recorded. The Inquirer's February 2024 list placed a fridge at Blackwell Library (125 S 52nd St); that was not checked against the group's current list.

records.name: Germantown Community Fridge
records.summary: Neighbors who keep two free community fridges stocked in Germantown. They take donations, make sandwiches, clean the fridges, and tend a small garden in warm months.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for fridge cleaning shifts, make sandwiches for grab and go drop offs, pick up donations by car, do a grocery run (up to $100, reimbursed), or help in the garden on High Street from spring through fall.

schedule.text: The fridges are open 24 hours a day, every day. Cleaning shifts are on a SignUpGenius sheet, and the garden runs from spring through fall.

first_step.how: Fill in the 'Volunteer With Us!' form linked from the group's site, or email germantownfridge@gmail.com
first_step.basis: A public volunteer form and email, with several roles listed, but the page does not describe training or a first shift

records.notes: The site's only dated item is a 2024 copyright footer, which does not count as evidence. Home-cooked meals must be labeled with an expiration date and ingredients. The grocery reimbursement steps are on a separate grocery page that was not read.

records.name: South Philadelphia Community Fridge
records.summary: A food-sharing project that keeps community fridges and pantry shelves stocked at eight sites across South Philadelphia, with a volunteer list for cleaning, driving and fundraising help.
records.what_you_do: Clean and organize fridges and pantries, drive large food donations, meet donation drivers, buy groceries with donated money, represent the project at community events, or help with social media, graphic design or grant writing.

schedule.text: The fridges and pantries are open and accessible 24 hours a day, every day, as the group states.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer list form linked from the group's take action page, or email southphlcommunityfridge@gmail.com
first_step.basis: A public volunteer list and email, with several needs listed, but the page gives no training or shift details

records.notes: The site names a fiscal sponsor, The Hack Foundation, and prints an EIN (81-2908499) for it. That EIN belongs to the sponsor, so it is not written as this group's EIN. The site's copyright footer (2025) does not count as evidence. The February 2024 Inquirer list named different host sites, so only the group's own list is used.

records.name: Broad Street Love
records.summary: A ministry on South Broad Street in Center City that serves a sit-down weekday lunch to more than 300 guests, runs a clothing boutique, and offers personal care items. It was formerly Broad Street Ministry.
records.what_you_do: Help serve lunch in the dining room on weekdays, or help with the clothing boutique. Volunteers start with an orientation and must be able to stand and move comfortably for several hours.

schedule.text: Lunch is served Monday to Friday, 11:30 am to 1:15 pm. Meal service volunteers work Monday to Friday, 10:15 am to 2 pm.

first_step.how: Register for a meal service shift on the volunteer calendar at broadstreetlove.volunteerhub.com/vv2/. Volunteers must be 16 or older.
first_step.basis: Shifts are open to the public on a sign-up calendar and volunteers begin with an orientation, though the page does not say beginners are welcome

records.notes: Renamed from Broad Street Ministry; the old domain redirects to broadstreetlove.org. The donation mailing address is PO Box 22656, Philadelphia, PA 19110, which is not a place to visit. The meal volunteer page asks people who need community service or court-mandated hours to contact the group before signing up, so court_ordered_ok stays unknown. The page describes lunch as open to all.

records.name: Philabundance
records.summary: A regional food bank that supplies community partners across Philadelphia and nearby counties in Pennsylvania and New Jersey. Volunteers can pack and sort food, cook in its community kitchen, or make cards from home.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a packing and sorting shift, help prepare meals in the community kitchen, or make cards for the Notes of Sunshine project and mail them to the volunteer department.

schedule.text: Packing, sorting and community kitchen shifts are offered each week. The volunteer pages do not list set days or times.

first_step.how: Sign up for a shift on the volunteer portal at philabundance.volunteerhub.com/vv2/, or email volunteer@philabundance.org
first_step.basis: Open sign-up on a public portal and by email; the page does not describe training or a first-visit step

records.notes: The site shows no dated items, so status is probably_active. The supporting community partners page says Philabundance can no longer provide documentation for court-ordered community service, so court_ordered_ok stays unknown. The volunteer page also lists warehouse repack shifts at a Hunger Relief Center in South Philadelphia with no street address; that was not made a separate record. The Find Food page and the partner search need a browser or map and were skipped. The community partners page did not show partner names in its text, so no partner pantries are recorded.

records.name: Northwest Mutual Aid Collective
records.summary: A volunteer group that works against hunger and food waste. Volunteers rescue surplus groceries, pack bags for neighbors, and bring meals to older and disabled residents.
records.what_you_do: Help in the warehouse by receiving, storing and checking the dates on donations (lifting up to 50 lbs), pack grocery bags, help with office tasks, or drive meals to seniors and disabled neighbors (a valid driver's license and car insurance are needed).

first_step.how: Call 484-640-2792 or email info@northwestmutualaidcollective.org to ask about the roles listed on the volunteer page. The warehouse does not accept mail, so use these contacts.
first_step.basis: Roles are listed publicly, but the page gives no sign-up steps, shift times or training information

records.notes: The site names no city, neighborhood or shift times. The Philadelphia warehouse address comes from its Contact Us page. The Inquirer's January 2025 guide lists it among Philadelphia groups. The second phone number on the contact page is 267-385-7163. The site's Programs page was not read.

records.name: Philly Unknown Project
records.summary: A grassroots nonprofit that does hand to hand outreach on the street in Kensington and wider Philadelphia. It hands out bags with snacks, socks, hygiene supplies and resource information, and it runs the Ruth Street Garden.
records.what_you_do: Help with outreach, pack compassion bags, support the group's initiatives and events, work at the hub, or pick up donations.

first_step.how: Use the 'Become A Volunteer Today' link on the site, which opens an email to phillyunknownproject@gmail.com
first_step.basis: A public volunteer email; the page lists roles but no schedule, training or first-shift steps

records.notes: Donations go through Givebutter. The site's only date is a 2025 footer copyright, which does not count as evidence. The group lists no meal program; snacks are one item in its bags. The Ruth Street Garden and mural work were described on the homepage only and were not visited.

leads_only.name: Collective Success Network
leads_only.note: Named in the Inquirer January 2025 mutual aid guide with an online volunteer application and donation options. Mailing address is in Flourtown (Montgomery County). No website link in the guide and Philadelphia service not confirmed.

leads_only.name: Homies Helping Homies
leads_only.note: Idealist listing only. Neighborhoods named as Point Breeze and Gray's Ferry. No own website linked and no street address. Not recorded because Idealist is a lead platform.

leads_only.name: Love Your Neighbor Philly
leads_only.note: Started by Temple students. Named in a February 2021 Temple News article with no website or current contact in the article, so likely dormant. Not recorded.

leads_only.name: Philly We Rise
leads_only.note: Named in a search result as an organizers' resource guide that started in the COVID era. Its site was not confirmed or checked.

leads_only.name: Fridges and Family
leads_only.note: Instagram only in the Inquirer February 2024 fridge list. Fridges at 1149 S 9th St and 1940 Liacouras Walk (Temple). Platform lead, not checked.

leads_only.name: East Falls Community Fridge
leads_only.note: Instagram only in the Inquirer February 2024 fridge list. Fridge at Vault + Vine, 3507 Midvale Ave. Platform lead, not checked.

leads_only.name: Northern Liberties Neighbors Association
leads_only.note: Hosts the Mama-Tee fridge at 700 N 3rd St. No own website was found in the sources read.

Coral Street Fridge. The domain does not resolve (DNS lookup failed). The February 2024 Inquirer list placed a fridge at LAVA Space, 4134 Lancaster Ave. Not recorded.
Double Trellis (West Philadelphia meal prep per the Inquirer guide). Both this page and the root page return 404, so it was not recorded.
Prevention Point Philadelphia volunteer page. Blocked, not recorded.
Operation Save Our City. The TLS certificate does not match the domain, so the site was not read. The Inquirer guide lists an 856 area code phone. Not recorded.
Ronald McDonald House Charities of Philadelphia (family lodging near hospitals, not food access). Blocked, not recorded.
Free Library guide to community fridges. Blocked, so its fridge list was not used.
Link given in the Inquirer guide. Returns 404. The group's homepage was read instead.

notes: Budget: all 3 WebSearch calls were used, which reached the cap. 39 WebFetch calls were used of 60. The searches covered community fridge lists, a mutual aid directory, and food rescue and coalition contacts. The Inquirer mutual aid guide (dated January 14, 2025) was the only dated source for several groups, so most statuses are probably_active. Coverage gaps: the Share and Philabundance locator tools were skipped (browser tools) as instructed. The Share Find Food page is not a block, but it has no written partner list. The Philabundance partner list did not come through in page text, so no partner pantries are recorded. Dropped with reason (not written as records): StudentsCare (its page describes a Florida-based buddy program with no Philadelphia or Penn content, and it is not a food group); Philadelphia Community Bail Fund (not food access, for the justice lane); Unity Java (cafe site, no fridge page; the commUNITY Fridge it hosts is not recorded); Friends Select School (a school that hosts a fridge, not a separate group); Generocity 2020 and PhillyVoice 2022 lists (too old to show activity); Next City article (background only). Coalition Against Hunger: the domain now serves casino content, so someone should check the real organization by hand before anyone contacts it. Mama-Tee and The People's Fridge share several fridge sites; both records are kept because each has its own volunteer or pop-up path.
